llm.summary: Today is a two-headed event day: Nvidia reports after the close into the worst AI-sentiment backdrop of the cycle (Jensen Huang's exit, a Dec. 1 House hearing, an export-control panel, Eisman calling neoclouds 'in big trouble'), while Anthropic is set to price its IPO above the $70-78 range. The macro has flipped from 'cuts' to 'hikes': inflation printed 3.7% with strategists talking 4%, the 10-year sits near 5.1%, St. Louis Fed's Musalem floated four more hikes, and Cleveland's president prefers 'small rate hikes.' That rate shock is doing real damage beneath the index: semis and AI hardware were hit hard (MU -8%, LRCX -7%, MRVL -7%, Dell -7%, INTC -7%, AMD -6%, AMAT -5%, Vertiv -7%), gold is at a 14-month low near $3,850, bitcoin broke $65K, and banks are curbing AI debt exposure. The real economy is bifurcating: October retail sales were merely in line at +0.2%, Home Depot showed spending up but traffic weak, and homebuilder sentiment collapsed to a 14-year low with nearly half of builders cutting prices. Flows confirm the rotation — Health Care, Staples and Financials accelerating, Technology at -67, Value beating Growth by 101 points. Our portfolio is positioned on the right side of that rotation (insurers, managed care, distribution, pharma), with the exposed edges being MAS (housing), BBY (gapping -4.2%) and DAL (discretionary consumer). The key question for the next month is not whether AI demand is real but whether it can be financed at a 5% long rate — that, not Nvidia's quarter, is what breaks or extends the trade.

market_thesis.short_term: Event-driven, two-sided and fragile. Nvidia's print can produce a violent relief rally in a deeply de-risked AI complex, but the rate backdrop caps any rebound: a 5.1% 10-year with hike talk is a valuation ceiling, not a floor. Expect continued dispersion — defensives and value grinding higher, high-multiple AI hardware and long-duration speculative assets (crypto, neoclouds, unprofitable growth) remaining the funding source. Base case: index chop, violent single-name moves, leadership stays in Health Care/Staples/Financials.
market_thesis.medium_term: Stagflation and Reflation each carry ~34% odds and both are rising at the expense of Goldilocks — that argues for owning cash-generative, pricing-power businesses and real-economy earners over duration. The AI capex cycle does not stop, but its financing gets scrutinized: banks pulling back on AI debt, neocloud spreads widening, and Anthropic's IPO becoming the market's referendum on private-AI marks. Housing is the clearest cyclical casualty at 5%+ mortgage-linked rates; builders cutting prices and buying down rates means margin compression flows through to building products. Expect broadening into small caps and value to persist as long as nominal growth stays firm.
market_thesis.long_term: The structural AI build-out — compute, power, grid, fabs, cooling — is a decade-long capital cycle that survives this drawdown; the equity leadership of it rotates from merchant GPU sellers to the electricity, networking, memory and physical-infrastructure layer. Alongside it: a persistently higher cost of capital re-prices everything financed with cheap money (housing, private credit, speculative tech), rewards balance-sheet strength, and makes insurance float, healthcare demographics and energy/hard-asset supply the durable compounders. Deglobalization and reshoring keep goods inflation stickier than the pre-2020 norm.

short_term: Consumers are trading down and shopping on value: retail sales only +0.2%, Home Depot reporting spending up but traffic weak, and skepticism about whether Amazon's Black Friday deals are real discounts — people are spending but auditing every dollar.

Would-be homebuyers are striking: builders are cutting prices and buying down mortgage rates to manufacture affordability, meaning the household is now negotiating from strength on shelter for the first time in years.
Retail investors are buying the AI dip reflexively ($1.6bn into Nvidia despite the selloff) while professionals de-risk — a classic late-cycle split in who owns the risk.
Savers are re-anchoring to a 5% risk-free rate: with inflation at 3.7%, cash and short Treasuries are a live competitor to both gold and bitcoin, which is why both broke down.
Households are substituting convenience for cost at the margin (DIY lunch 'hacks' over the $20 desk salad) — small but telling behavioural trade-down in daily spend.
Investors are rotating attention from growth narratives to income and safety: Health Care, Staples and Financials flows accelerating, dividend and 'buy and hold forever' content rising.
long_term: People want security over optionality when money costs 5%: insurance, healthcare access, staples and guaranteed income gain permanent share of wallet and portfolio.

Energy is becoming a consumer-facing political issue — 'when the lights dim' electricity-price discourse and rising searches on AI data-center water/power use mean the public now links AI to their utility bill. That is a constraint on where compute gets built.

Access to the AI equity story is being democratized (Anthropic courting retail in its IPO, tokenized stock trading arriving) — status and participation, not just returns, drive flows into these assets.

Housing demand is being structurally deferred, not destroyed: a cohort is re-allocating to renting, storage and experiences while shelter costs stay unaffordable — supporting Public Storage-type assets and travel over first-time-buyer formation.

Work and knowledge are being re-tooled around agents: enterprises are shifting from headcount growth to software leverage, which is why cost-cut stories (Disney's $3bn target) are rewarded over revenue-growth stories.
National energy sovereignty is now a mainstream consumer and political preference — nuclear re-adoption across Asia, Japan's 'Asian IEA' proposal, Philippine reserve-building.
